name: Tokyo
title: Family holidays in Tokyo
intro: Bullet trains, robots and the friendliest city you'll ever visit with children. Here's what Tokyo is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 8 to 9 hrs ahead of the UK

facts_note: UK plugs need an adapter. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Late March and early April bring the cherry blossom and the biggest crowds. October and November are mild with autumn leaves and fewer people. Summer is hot and humid, but there are festivals and fireworks, and winter is cold, dry and sunny.

things.name: teamLab Planets
things.blurb: Walk barefoot through water and light. Book ahead.

things.name: Ghibli Museum
things.blurb: A dreamy museum for Totoro fans. Tickets go on sale monthly and sell out fast.

things.name: Senso-ji Temple
things.blurb: Tokyo's oldest temple, with snack stalls all the way up to it.

things.name: Shibuya Crossing
things.blurb: Watch the world's busiest crossing from above, then join in.

things.name: Ueno Park and Zoo
things.blurb: Giant pandas, museums and boats on the pond in one big park.

things.name: Tokyo Disneyland & DisneySea
things.blurb: Two parks by the bay. DisneySea is one of the best in the world.

faqs.question: Is Tokyo good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Very. It's safe, spotless and easy on public transport, and children love the food, trains and gadgets. Big stations are busy, so use a pushchair-friendly route or a sling.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Seven to ten nights covers Tokyo and a day trip or two. Many families add Kyoto by bullet train.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days without a visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: Is Tokyo expensive?
faqs.answer: Less than you might think. The yen has been weak against the pound, and food from convenience stores and noodle shops is cheap and good.
